item.title: Follow next_cursor in listItems
item.brief: In inventory-client, make listItems(transport) follow next_cursor per the shared contract until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged, first request with no cursor, and returning all items in order. Add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a single page, and an absent next_cursor. Update the README to document that listItems pages through the API. Keep npm test passing. Commit the change on the branch; do not push.

agt_01M8AVC6AZXA7GNT6PKPDCBA9S:1.description: Cycle guard only catches a next_cursor equal to the cursor just sent (A→A). A longer loop (A→B→A) would still page forever. Consider tracking a Set of seen cursors.

agt_01M8AVC6AZXA7GNT6PKPDCBA9S:2.description: If the response body is null or not an object, `body.items` throws a raw TypeError before the friendly 'no items array' error. Harmless but the guard could check body first.

agt_01M8AVC6AZXA7GNT6PKPDCBA9S:3.description: Verified on this branch: npm test gives 7 pass, 0 fail. The multi-page and repeated-cursor tests would fail against the base listItems (base sends no cursor and returns only the first page, and never rejects). The null and absent next_cursor tests pass on both, which is acceptable as regression guards.

agt_01M8AVC6AZXA7GNT6PKPDCBA9S:4.description: README wording matches the implementation: first request has no cursor, the cursor is passed back unchanged, and paging stops on null or absent. The README does not mention the repeated-cursor rejection, which is a minor doc gap.

agt_01M8AVDHYMSVV0MS7R0A05T40J:1.description: Finding :1 is fixed: a Set of seen cursors rejects a repeated next_cursor, and the test covers a multi-page cycle (c1->c2->c1). Finding :2 is fixed: the body is checked for null and non-object before the items check, and the test covers a null body. Finding :4 is fixed: the README now states the repeated-cursor error rule. Finding :3 is verification only and needs no code change. npm test passes 9

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in one client function that every listItems caller uses; tests cover paging edge cases; no network, auth or persistence change. Reviewers rated medium; the final README-only delta was rated low.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor query params, body {items, next_cursor}, items ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page, HTTP 400 with {error} for invalid limit or cursor. Validate inputs at the boundary, keep functions small, add tests for paging, the last page, bad limit/cursor and default limit. Update the README to document the new parameters and response. Keep python3 -m unittest passing. Commit the change on the branch; do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

pr.body: Approach: api.py list_items parses limit and cursor via small helpers that raise BadRequest; list_items maps that to 400 {error}. The cursor is the decimal id of the last item on the page; the next page is items with a greater id, so paging stays stable as ids are unique. A non-object query returns 400. Files: api.py, test_api.py (11 paging, bounds, error, edge-case tests), README.md (parameters and response). Checks: python3 -B -m unittest, 14 tests OK at a4b1dba. Review: reviewer-1 and reviewer-2 passed the whole change at 77bbac5; reviewer-3 failed it on a non-dict query and was fixed in 8580ad1 (Review-Fix trailer); reviewer-delta passed that delta; reviewer-delta-2 passed a4b1dba as a delta from 8580ad1. Open follow-ups (non-blocking): parse helpers carry no assertions; falsy non-dict query values return the default page as at base; cursor format is an id, documented as unstable; inventory-client not in this stage.

risk.why: Public API change: new limit and cursor params and a new {items, next_cursor} body. Default page of 20 changes what existing GET /items callers receive, as the shared contract requires. The fix commit and docs commit are low risk on their own.

pr.summary: GET /items now pages: limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor. now returns {items, next_cursor}, ordered by id. before: all items in one response, now: at most 20 by default, next_cursor null on the last page, 400 {error} on invalid limit/cursor.
